dispatch.summary: The papal Secretary of State's counter-order to the nuncio at Innsbruck, where the Emperor had fled: instead of asking for his passports after Lützow's departure from Rome, he is to remain with the Emperor wherever he goes, and show the dispatch at once to Mgr Morichini. Printed in cipher by Mazzini's L'Italia del Popolo (30 June 1848) and posted by Klaus Schmeh as unsolved; the key was recovered here, some code words remain unread ([8xxx]).
dispatch.en:
By my (letter) of [8734][8760][8904][8739][8413] you were instructed that, following the orders given to His Excellency
the (Signor) [8227] di Lützow to leave Rome, you should likewise ask for your passports so as to return to the capital,
or to go to (Cologne), which (is) (far) from the (war), (as) [8704]e, you had thought it fitting. (However), because of
new circumstances that have arisen, I inform you [8093][8102] of the (Holy Father) that you remain at Innsbruck with the
Emperor and wherever he may go; the decision [8136] indicated, concerning the request for passports, being understood
as suspended: it matters [8131] to the (Holy Father) (this) new instruction, which is sent to you by three different
routes (in order to) ensure its arrival.

(clear:) To save time you must with all speed make the present despatch available for inspection (cipher:)

snip.cap: The Roman reprint of L'Italia del Popolo, 30 June 1848: the clear opening of Cardinal Soglia's dispatch and the first lines of digits, 5 the word break, 8XXX the code
snip.credit: Tony Gaffney, via Klaus Schmeh, Cipherbrain

system: Two-digit 64-cell table of letters, homophones and syllables over digits {0,1,2,3,4,6,7,9}, 5 as word separator, 8XXX one-part alphabetical code for words, lone 1-4 as punctuation.
